FOREWORD This Indian Standard (Part 2/See 14) (First Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Ceramicware Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council. This standard was first published in 1968. The Committee while reviewing IS 3972: 1968 decided to publish this standard in two parts. Part 1 deals with production of specimens for testing in two sections, namely, Section 1 Enamel led sheet steel, and Section 2 Enamelled cast iron. Pall 2 deals with various test methods applicable to vitreous enamelled sheet steel and vitreous enamelled cast iron. The Committee also decided that Part 2 shall have various sections and each section will deal with a particular test method. This standard prescribes the method for determination Part 2 are as follows: Section 1 of adherence of vitreous enamelware. The other sections of

Resistance to citric acid at room temperature and boiling temperature Low and high voltage test for detection and locating defects

Section 2 Section 3
Section 4 Section 5 Section 6 Section 7 Section 8 Section 9 Section 11 Section 12 Section 13

Resistance to boiling water and water vapour
Resistance to thermal shock Resistance to hot alkali (sodium hydroxide Reflectance and specular gloss acid

Resistance to boiling hydrochloric Resistance to heat

Resistance to dilute sulphuric acid at room temperature . Resistance to abrasion Resistance to torsion Resistance to warpage

Two methods have been described for evaluating the adherence of vitreous enamels and ceramic coatings to sheet metal. Of these, the so called `drop ball method' shall be used as a routine method and the other method using adherence meter shall be the referee method. The composition of the Committee responsible for formulation of this standard is given in Annex A,

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2: 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)'. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

6 TEST

METHOD

Two methods have been described for evaluating the adherence of vitreous enamels and ceramic coatings to sheet metal. Of these, the so called `drop ball method' specified in 6.1 shall be used as a routine method, the method described in 6.2, which uses adherence meter, shall be the referee method. 6.1 Impact Resistance of Vitreous Enamelled Wares This method covers a procedure for determining the impact
resistance of vitreous enamel led wares.

6.1.3.1 Levelling impact machine -- Place the impact machine on a firm foundation, and, using the bubble level as a guide, level the machine by means of the three levelling screws. Tighten the nuts on the levelling against the machine base to lock the levelling screw in position. 6.1.3.2 Adjustment of guide tube -- Rotate the 91 cm guide tube (after loosening the clamps) until the two notches at the bottom of the tube are in a line, parallel to the fi-ont of the machine. Raise or lower the guide-tube, if necessary, so that two clamps fall between perforations in the tube; then tighten the clamps to hold the guide-tube in position. Raise the guide-tube assembly by lifting the bottom clamp support, and swing to one side. This operation places the guide-tube out of the way of the 1

1S 3972 (Part 2/See 14) :2007 may be necessary to move the guide-tube to or away from the support rod until the guide-tube is approximately centered above the bottom radius of the utensil. This is done by loosening the set screw holding the guide-tubeclamp extension arms, moving the guide-tube, checking to see that the guide-tube is vertical, and tightening the set screws. To permit both the backward or forward, and the raising or lowering, tine adjustment movements of the guide-tube assembly, loosen the set screws in the support rod base and in the sliding-clamp support stop. The correct point of impact on wares which have a bottom radius of less than 13 mm and a bottom diameter of not over 178 mm maybe obtained by either one of the following two methods: a) Place the impact locator across the bottom of the ware, with the short arm resting upon the bottom radius directly below the guide-tube. Lower the guide-tube by the fine adjustment setter until it nearly touches the bottom radius of the ware. Move the guide-tube to or away from the front of the machine, as required, until the notches inthe bottom 6.1.3.5 Posi~ioning the ja[ling weight -- Place one of the two falling weight release pins through the set of perforations at a level of 125 mm below the specified minimum height of impact, the utensil must pass, and drop the falling weight into the tube. Place the second release pin in the set of perforations directly above `the falling weight now resting. 6.1.4 Procedure 6.1.4.1 Begin the test by pulling the lower release pin, which allows the falling weight to strike the bottom radius of the ware at the correct point of contact. Again drop the falling weight into the guide-tube, and place the previously pulled release pin in the next set of perforations above the now resting falling weight. Continue this procedure until the first chip visible to the normal eye at the distance of 44 mm occurs upon the enamelled surface of the utensil. At this point, note the perforation directly below the release pin remaining in the guide-tube, and record as the failure point, in millimetres, for this particular point on the ware. 6.1.4.2 Move the rotating disc until the next groove lies in front of the guide-tube support rod, adjust the guidetube, if necessary, to provide the correct point of impact, and again follow the above procedure, always starting the test by releasing the falling weight from the set of perforations at a level of 125 mm below the specified minimum height of impact the utensil shall pass. Repeat this procedure until ten points on the bottom radius of the utensil have been tested, and have or have not failed at some set of perforations within the length of the 91 mm guide-tube. 6.1.4.3 One complete impact test consists in testing each of five identical utensils as directed above for a total of 50 tested points. 6.1.5 Calculations and Report

of the guide-tube are in line with the point of contact
between the bottom radius of the ware and the short arm of the impact point locator. Tighten the set screws on the guide-tube support rod base to lock the support rod in position; then raise the guidetube to a point 3 mm above the point of impact on the utensil, and lock in a position by tightening the set screw in the sliding clamp support stop. Tighten the set screw in the lower clamp support to prevent a sideways motion of the guide-tube. b) Raise the guide-tube to a point 3 mm above the point of impact on the utensil and tighten both the set screw in the sliding clamp support stop and the set screw in the lower clamp support. Place the impact weight on the bottom radius of the ware directly below, and inside the bottom of the guidetube. Move the guide tube to or away from the front of the machine, until the impact weight just remains in place. Then tighten the support rod base set screws to lock the guide-tube in position. When round-shaped wires are tested, move the guide-tube to, or away ffom, the front of the machine, and raise or lower the guide-tube a small amount to obtain the correct point of impact for each t~st point; this adjustment is necessary, as the test specimen is centered only approximately on the rotating disk, and some wares are not true in shape. When oval, square or rectangular wares are tested, move the ware itself for nearly every test point, and adjust the guide-tube for the correct point of impact at each test point.
NOTE -- When returning the guide-tube to its normal or working position, do not force the lower clamp support down upon the guide key, but let it settle into position of its own accord.

Take the average of the ten tests on each utensil as the impact resistance of that particular utensil. Report the average of five identical utensil averages often points each as the impact resistance value for the enamel. 6.2 Adherence Meter Method

This method is not applicable to metals over 2 mm or under 0.4 mm in thickness, nor to vitreous enamels on aluminium or aluminium alloys. Some anomalies have also been noted in certain processes in which the cover coat is applied directly to sheet steel. Processes used in applying the cover coat directly to sheet steel might require a different rating criterion from that used in evaluating conventional ground coats on steel. 6.2.1 Apparatus Adherence meter is to be obtained from Porcelain Enamel Institute (PEI), USA, or from their authorized agents. 3

IS 3972 (Part 2/See 14) :2007 6.2.1.1 Die depth 6.2.4 Adherence Measurements

Dies of different depths are used for specimens of different metal thickness. Details regarding these dies are shown in Table 1. 6.2.1.2 Adherence meter

6.2.4.1 Remove a portion of the enamel fkom a comer of the specimen to expose metal for attaching the spring clip ground wire to the exposed metal. 6.2.4.2 Allow 5 min to warm up the electronic components. Raise the test head on the elevator post by means of the elevator knob. Place the specimen holder in position. With the concave side up, place the specimen on the specimen holder with the deformation centered in the hole in the spring supported plunger. Rotate the probe cluster to initial position by pushing the pivot knob to the left. Lower the test head until the probes contact the specimen and the plastic guard ring rests firmly on the specimen. 6.2.4.3 Counter is set at the zero position. Attach the spring clip of ground wire to the exposed metal. Press the pushbutton starting switch momentarily and observe the red and green lights on the circuit box, The green light should be lighted when the power is on, but the meter is not in operation. The red light should be lighted momentarily after the momentary starting switch is pressed. When the measurement in initial position has been completed, record the counter reading and reset the counter to zero. 6.2.4.4 Raise the test head and rotate the probe cluster to the next position (centre), Lower the head and repeat the procedure described in 6.2.4.3. This is repeated again with the probe cluster in another fixed position, Thus three readings on the same specimen are obtained. 6.2.5 Calculations for Single Determination

Itis essentially an electronic instrument equipped with 169 needle-like probes assembled in hexagonal pattern 30.7 mm across the flats and 35.6 mm across the comers. Each probe is connected to an electric circuit, which may be completed through the grounded base metal of the specimen. 6.2.2 Test Specimens

These shall be prepared as in 5. 6.2.2.1 The test specimens consist of enamelled panels not less than 10 cm in size. These specimens shall be prepared by enameling seven different metal blanks and not by cutting tlom a single enamelled sheet. 6.2,2,2 The test specimens shall have the type, thickness, and number of coatings representing commercial practice for the specific enamels involved. The thickness of the enamel or each specimen shall be measured at the spot to be deformed. 6.2.3 Deforming Test Specimens

6.2.3.1 The die shaIl be cleaned with a small brush before each deforming operation. 6.2.3.2 Each specimen shall be deformed at the centre.

6.2.3.3 The specimen shall be placed on the deforming die mounted on the ram of the hydraulic jack and the motion of the jack will force the specimen against the stationary steel ball centered above the die, thus deforming the specimen. 6,2.3.4 The specimen is deformed by full length strokes of the hydraulic jack at a rate that will consume 5 s from the time deformation starts until 140 kg/cm2 pressure is obtained. This pressure is maintained for 5 s and then released. 6.2.3.5 For specimen having metal thickness between 2 mm and 1.37 mm a circle should be marked with a glass marking pencil around the end of the plastic shield while the specimen is being held at 140 kg/cm2 pressure. This circle shall be used to centre the specimen in the adherence meter. 6.2.3.6 The deformed specimen should be cleaned of loose fragments by twice dropping the specimen, face down, from a height of 15 cm. 4

6.2.5.1 One sample consists of seven specimens. Average the values obtained at the three angular positions of the probe cluster, to obtain the meter reading, ~, for each individual specimen. Use the arithmetic mean, ~, of the seven individual values, X, as the meter reading of the sample. 6.2.5.2 Adherence also Table 2): A . index, A, is calculated as follows (see
